# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act originally set 2 August 2026 as the application date for high-risk AI system obligations under Annex III (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence); [AI Act Law](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)). However, following the "Digital Omnibus on AI," this date has been postponed to **2 December 2027** (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation); [EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)). Many secondary sources have not yet been updated to reflect this change, creating a significant information gap in public-facing compliance guidance (medium confidence) ([artificialintelligenceact.eu](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline)).

## Key Findings

**Original Timeline (2024 Adoption)**
As originally adopted in 2024, the AI Act stipulated that Annex III high-risk obligations would become applicable 36 months after entry into force, i.e., 2 August 2026 (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence); [Goodwin Law](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline)). The Act is reported to have entered into force on 1 August 2024, though this specific date carries only low confidence given limited source corroboration ([CSA Labs](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20)).

**The Digital Omnibus Amendment**
The European Commission proposed a "Digital Omnibus on AI" to delay Annex III application by up to 16 months, contingent on confirming that necessary standards and conformity-assessment tools were available (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)). This proposal was adopted on 19 November 2025, reached political agreement between Council and Parliament on 7 May 2026, and entered into force on 27 July 2026 (medium confidence) ([Digital Strategy EC](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)).

**Current Application Date: 2 December 2027**
Following the Omnibus, Annex III high-risk obligations now apply from **2 December 2027**, as confirmed by multiple official EU sources (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation); [Digital Strategy EC](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). The consolidated EUR-Lex text (version dated 27.07.2026) corroborates this, confirming Chapter III, Sections 1-3 (covering Annex III obligations) apply from this later date rather than 2 August 2026 (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727); [AI Act Law](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)). Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 is cited as the legal instrument fixing this date, though this specific citation carries low confidence due to limited corroboration ([AnnexOps](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027)).

**Related Deadlines**
High-risk obligations for AI embedded in regulated products (Annex I) apply from 2 August 2028 (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation)). Transparency obligations under Article 50 generally apply from 2 August 2026, with a transitional deadline of 2 December 2026 for legacy systems (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/faq)). Providers of high-risk systems already on the market before the Annex III date are only covered if those systems undergo significant design changes afterward, though systems intended for public authorities must comply regardless (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties

Several sources have not been updated to reflect the Omnibus amendment and continue to state 2 August 2026 as the Annex III deadline, directly contradicting official EU guidance now confirming 2 December 2027 (medium confidence) ([artificialintelligenceact.eu](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline); [CSA Labs](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20)).

Sources also disagree on the Annex I deadline, with most indicating 2028 while one states 2027—this discrepancy is unresolved ([Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/artificial-intelligence/ai-governance/eu-ai-act) vs. [Digital Strategy EC](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)).

**Low-confidence claim flagged:** One news blog claims a further delay to 2 August 2029 under an alleged "final text agreed in September 2026." This claim (confidence 0.12) is uncorroborated by any official source, including the EUR-Lex consolidated text, and should be treated as unreliable ([news blog](https://ai-act-news-blog.example/annex-iii-deadline-update)).

## Knowledge Gaps
- Whether the 2 December 2027 date is a fixed backstop or remains conditional on Commission confirmation of standards readiness.
- The precise scope of "significant design changes" triggering earlier compliance obligations for legacy systems.
- Resolution of the Annex I deadline discrepancy (2027 vs. 2028).
- Whether further legislative amendments could adjust the 2 December 2027 date before it takes effect.

# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act originally set 2 August 2026 as the application date for high-risk AI system obligations under Annex III (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence); [AI Act Law](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)). However, following the "Digital Omnibus on AI," this date has been postponed to **2 December 2027** (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation); [EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)). Many secondary sources have not yet been updated to reflect this change, creating a significant information gap in public-facing compliance guidance (medium confidence) ([artificialintelligenceact.eu](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline)).

## Key Findings

**Original Timeline (2024 Adoption)**
As originally adopted in 2024, the AI Act stipulated that Annex III high-risk obligations would become applicable 36 months after entry into force, i.e., 2 August 2026 (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence); [Goodwin Law](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline)). The Act is reported to have entered into force on 1 August 2024, though this specific date carries only low confidence given limited source corroboration ([CSA Labs](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20)).

**The Digital Omnibus Amendment**
The European Commission proposed a "Digital Omnibus on AI" to delay Annex III application by up to 16 months, contingent on confirming that necessary standards and conformity-assessment tools were available (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)). This proposal was adopted on 19 November 2025, reached political agreement between Council and Parliament on 7 May 2026, and entered into force on 27 July 2026 (medium confidence) ([Digital Strategy EC](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)).

**Current Application Date: 2 December 2027**
Following the Omnibus, Annex III high-risk obligations now apply from **2 December 2027**, as confirmed by multiple official EU sources (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation); [Digital Strategy EC](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). The consolidated EUR-Lex text (version dated 27.07.2026) corroborates this, confirming Chapter III, Sections 1-3 (covering Annex III obligations) apply from this later date rather than 2 August 2026 (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727); [AI Act Law](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)). Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 is cited as the legal instrument fixing this date, though this specific citation carries low confidence due to limited corroboration ([AnnexOps](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027)).

**Related Deadlines**
High-risk obligations for AI embedded in regulated products (Annex I) apply from 2 August 2028 (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation)). Transparency obligations under Article 50 generally apply from 2 August 2026, with a transitional deadline of 2 December 2026 for legacy systems (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/faq)). Providers of high-risk systems already on the market before the Annex III date are only covered if those systems undergo significant design changes afterward, though systems intended for public authorities must comply regardless (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties

Several sources have not been updated to reflect the Omnibus amendment and continue to state 2 August 2026 as the Annex III deadline, directly contradicting official EU guidance now confirming 2 December 2027 (medium confidence) ([artificialintelligenceact.eu](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline); [CSA Labs](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20)).

Sources also disagree on the Annex I deadline, with most indicating 2028 while one states 2027—this discrepancy is unresolved ([Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/artificial-intelligence/ai-governance/eu-ai-act) vs. [Digital Strategy EC](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)).

**Low-confidence claim flagged:** One news blog claims a further delay to 2 August 2029 under an alleged "final text agreed in September 2026." This claim (confidence 0.12) is uncorroborated by any official source, including the EUR-Lex consolidated text, and should be treated as unreliable ([news blog](https://ai-act-news-blog.example/annex-iii-deadline-update)).

## Knowledge Gaps
- Whether the 2 December 2027 date is a fixed backstop or remains conditional on Commission confirmation of standards readiness.
- The precise scope of "significant design changes" triggering earlier compliance obligations for legacy systems.
- Resolution of the Annex I deadline discrepancy (2027 vs. 2028).
- Whether further legislative amendments could adjust the 2 December 2027 date before it takes effect.
